items.headline: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images
items.excerpt: OpenAI's new ChatGPT Sketch mode lets you scribble a rough drawing and have Images 2.5 turn it into a detailed rendering, making a hand sketch part of the prompt. It pushes image generation toward the kind of sketch-and-refine loop designers already use.

items.headline: Meta bets on AI agent Muse to catch up in AI race
items.excerpt: Meta unveiled Muse, a consumer AI agent that can shop, send email and plan trips on a user's behalf, after spending billions overhauling its AI strategy. The launch is a bet that agent-first interfaces, not chat windows, are the next product surface.

items.headline: Autodesk's AI blueprint for CAD
items.excerpt: Autodesk has laid out its AI blueprint for CAD, pairing geometry-aware models with project-level intelligence inside Fusion. The aim is an assistant that understands parts and constraints rather than just text, reshaping how engineers and industrial designers iterate.

items.headline: Beyond headsets: Spatial computing's future
items.excerpt: As spatial computing matures past the headset, designers and engineers are being asked to adopt new ways of working to realise its potential. The piece argues the real shift is in review, collaboration and how 3D data is shared, not in the hardware.

items.headline: Blackmagic Design releases DaVinci Resolve 21.1
items.excerpt: Blackmagic has shipped DaVinci Resolve 21.1, a sizeable update to the free grading and editing app that adds an MCP server alongside new VFX and colour features. Exposing Resolve to AI agents over Model Context Protocol puts an agent directly inside a post-production timeline.

items.headline: New CG software you may have missed: 7 September 2026
items.excerpt: CG Channel's roundup covers nine tool updates, including JangaFX's real-time FX apps IlluGen and LiquiGen, the 3DGS Render add-on for Gaussian splats in Blender with real-time relighting, and Epic's RealityScan Mobile photogrammetry app. Most of the releases lean on AI-assisted capture, relighting or upscaling.

items.headline: This free app could become the Blender of texture painting software
items.excerpt: ArmorPaint 1.0 arrives after eight years in early access as a lightweight, open-source Substance Painter alternative available on every platform. The rewrite adds sculpting, UV editing and AI-based image upscaling plus photo-to-material generation.

items.headline: NVIDIA's RTX Spark showcase at IFA showed how DLSS is breaking out of gaming
items.excerpt: At IFA, NVIDIA demonstrated RTX Spark bringing DLSS 4.5 into Blender viewports rather than just games. Neural upscaling inside a DCC viewport means 3D artists get near-final-frame feedback while they model and light.

items.headline: Your AI-written brief might wreck your brand's chances of finding the right creatives
items.excerpt: Design agencies say AI-generated client briefs are flattening the signals they used to read when deciding which founders to take a chance on. The result is a hiring and pitching process that filters out exactly the interesting work it was meant to attract.

items.headline: Fovii showcases immersive videos and their creators on Apple Vision Pro
items.excerpt: The Fovii app on Apple Vision Pro offers a new platform to watch 180-degree immersive video and discover the creators behind each piece. It is one of the first distribution surfaces built specifically around immersive creators rather than flat catalogues.

items.headline: VRChat wins its first Emmy with immersive theatre production Uncanny Alley: A New Day
items.excerpt: VRChat has taken home its first Emmy, with the immersive theatre experience Uncanny Alley: A New Day winning Outstanding Emerging Media Program. It is a mainstream award validating social-VR spaces as a legitimate production medium.

items.headline: Quest's Meta Virtual Display gets a new name, input forwarding and Mac parity
items.excerpt: Meta's Quest virtual desktop feature has been renamed and now supports input forwarding, with the Mac version gaining functionality previously exclusive to Windows. For designers it edges headset-as-monitor closer to a usable daily workstation.

items.headline: Date Slop: building a deliberately bad UX with AI
items.excerpt: A developer entered a Bad UX competition for the worst possible date picker and used AI to build it. The exercise turns into a sharp read on how readily generative tools produce plausible-looking but hostile interface patterns.

items.headline: OpenAI brings template-based marketing design to ChatGPT with Adobe Express
items.excerpt: OpenAI is pulling template-based marketing design into ChatGPT through an Adobe Express plugin, letting users produce on-brand collateral without leaving the chat. It moves routine layout work out of design tools and into a conversational surface.

items.headline: The model is behaving impeccably. Your information architecture isn't.
items.excerpt: Using a 1960 study of how people draw city maps, the piece argues that most bad AI output is really an information-architecture failure. The model is legible only as far as the structure you hand it is legible.

items.headline: If you can externalize your design process, you can win back your time
items.excerpt: A practical look at using SKILL.md files to spell out the depth of your design work for teammates and for AI agents. Writing the process down turns tacit craft into something an agent can actually execute.
